checks.zero_instance_note: A check object with no instances belongs to a count=0 resource: the condition is defined in the configuration and there is no instance to evaluate it against. It is listed separately rather than folded into the pass count, because 'nothing was checked' is not 'the check passed'.

open_hazard_topic_policy_source_arn.finding: The guard's SNS topic policy admits cloudwatch.amazonaws.com to SNS:Publish under an ArnLike on aws:SourceArn naming exactly the guard's OWN THREE alarm ARNs. NONE of module.api's FOUR alarms is in that list, and infra/envs/demo passes that topic to them as var.alarm_actions.
open_hazard_topic_policy_source_arn.why_no_plan_can_settle_it: The policy's FIRST statement is SNS's own default idiom - Principal AWS:* narrowed by the condition AWS:SourceOwner = <this account> - and a same-account CloudWatch alarm may or may not be admitted by it. Deciding that requires an apply and a real breach, and no worker in this wave may apply anything.

both_outcomes_are_defects_and_they_are_o.admitted: all four demo-api alarms stop the demo. Three of them (-errors, -throttles, -duration-p99) are HEALTH signals, so this converts three health signals into self-inflicted outages. It is done deliberately under docs/leads/cost-finish-plan.md 0.5's ranking - an outage is recoverable by one command and a bill is not - and the one consequence that ranking does NOT excuse, a cold start tripping -duration-p99, is refused at plan time by the new floor precondition.
both_outcomes_are_defects_and_they_are_o.denied: all four carry an action SNS refuses. aws cloudwatch describe-alarms renders a denied publish identically to a delivered one, so this is a control that looks present and is not - the exact defect this wave exists to close, wearing a resource-policy hat.

open_hazard_topic_policy_source_arn.the_resolution_is_neither_of_the_two_obv: NOT unwiring module.api's alarms (that returns the demo to four actionless alarms) and NOT widening the topic policy's principal (that lets any same-account CloudWatch alarm stop the demo). It is for infra/modules/cost-guard to take an explicit list of ADDITIONAL publisher ARNs, which is that module's owner's change and not this worker's file.

falsification_of_the_module_cycle_rule.the_rule_that_survives: It is the SPLAT that is fatal, which is EXACTLY the rule infra/envs/demo/main.tf's header already recorded from 2026-08-10 - not a new one. A splat depends on the `module.api (close)` node, every alarm in that module feeds it, and those alarms now consume the guard's topic, so the loop closes. An indexed reference touches one output and its one resource. The local is kept anyway for three reasons that are NOT 'otherwise it cycles': [0] -> [*] is one refactor away and a constant cannot be splatted; the guard's name validation and its one IAM ARN become plan-time known independently of the api module, which is why guard_guarded_function_arn is a concrete string in this plan rather than (known after apply); and it is interface I6.

published_bounds.$comment: Read out of resource_changes for module.api[0].aws_lambda_function.this. Until this wave the six MAINLINE_* keys below were absent, so every one of those bounds was ENFORCED and UNREADABLE: an operator asking what response ceiling the function enforces had to unzip a 7.6 MB package and read a Python constant, because aws lambda get-function-configuration answered nothing. The application is authoritative and Terraform mirrors it - each value equals a named constant.
published_bounds.timeout_is_a_reliability_bound_not_a_spe: Lambda bills ACTUAL DURATION, so a 5.66 ms invocation costs exactly the same under a 14 s timeout as under a 3 s one: this number moves the bill by NOTHING. The 3 s that was requested is 0.80x the warm in-region gate_run p99 corrected to Lambda (3,729 ms) and would truncate the headline beat - the only beat that writes anything and the one on screen. 14 s is the smallest whole second that clears docs/deploy/LATENCY.md 5.1's binding case of 13,022.9 ms, by 1.07x.

duration_p99_band.floor_source: docs/deploy/LATENCY.md 5.1 binding case - cold start at 256 MB with a 2x worse tail
duration_p99_band.ceiling_source: timeout * 1000; Lambda caps the Duration datapoint at the timeout
duration_p99_band.why_the_floor_exists: The alarm now has an ACTION. Below the floor a COLD START - a judge's first click, not abuse and not an incident - would stop the demo until a human runs scripts/deploy/kill_switch.sh --restore.
duration_p99_band.why_the_floor_is_unconditional: It was FIRST WRITTEN conditional - `length(var.alarm_actions) == 0 || <the comparison>` - on the reasoning that an alarm which only REPORTS has no reason to carry a floor. THAT VERSION DID NOT FIRE, and it was caught by planting the violation rather than by reading the code. infra/envs/demo reaches the stop topic through try([module.guard[0].sns_topic_arn], []); try() returns a WHOLLY UNKNOWN value when its argument contains an unknown; so length(var.alarm_actions) is unknown at plan time, the whole || is unknown, and Terraform DEFERS an unknown precondition to apply instead of failing the plan. The plan says so in the open - all four demo-api alarms show alarm_actions = (known after apply). A precondition that cannot be evaluated at plan time is a control that looks present and is not, which is the exact defect this wave exists to close, so the guard clause was DELETED rather than repaired. The unconditional form reads two plain variables and is strictly TIGHTER than the one it replaces.
